clinicalPearls: Presents with painless, progressive enophthalmos and hypoglobus with facial asymmetry, in the absence of significant sinonasal symptoms
Results from gradual collapse of the maxillary sinus and downward bowing of the orbital floor rather than from a mass or trauma
The 'silent' label reflects the characteristic lack of sinusitis symptoms despite the underlying maxillary pathology
Ophthalmological features such as apparent enophthalmos, upper lid sulcus deepening, and lid retraction often bring the patient to attention first
CT is diagnostic, showing an opacified, contracted maxillary sinus with inward retraction of its walls and a depressed orbital floor
The initiating problem is occlusion of the osteomeatal complex producing negative intrasinus pressure and chronic atelectasis
Management combines endoscopic sinus surgery to restore maxillary ventilation with orbital floor reconstruction where enophthalmos is significant
reference.pathophysiology: Silent sinus syndrome, also termed chronic maxillary atelectasis, begins with obstruction of the maxillary sinus outflow at the osteomeatal complex. Trapped secretions are gradually resorbed and, with ventilation cut off, a persistent negative pressure develops within the sealed sinus. Over time this sub-atmospheric pressure draws the thin sinus walls inwards, so the antrum contracts and the orbital floor bows downward. Because the orbital floor descends and the maxillary volume falls, the orbital contents sink, producing the painless enophthalmos and hypoglobus that dominate the clinical picture, all typically without the pain or discharge of overt sinusitis.
additionalDifferentials: Orbital floor blow-out fracture with enophthalmos
Maxillary or sinonasal neoplasm causing orbital displacement
additionalInvestigations: CT of the sinuses and orbits, the key investigation demonstrating maxillary atelectasis and orbital floor depression
Nasal endoscopy to assess the middle meatus and osteomeatal complex
Ophthalmological assessment with measurement of enophthalmos and globe position
MRI where a neoplastic or soft-tissue cause needs exclusion
Comparison with old photographs to establish the acquired, progressive nature
redFlags: Rapidly progressive enophthalmos or proptosis suggesting a neoplastic process rather than atelectasis
Diplopia or restricted eye movements indicating significant orbital involvement
Visual disturbance requiring urgent ophthalmological assessment
Pain or destructive bony changes on imaging that are atypical and point to another diagnosis
reference.prognosis: The condition is benign and, once diagnosed, generally treated successfully by restoring maxillary ventilation, with orbital floor reconstruction correcting the enophthalmos; the cosmetic and functional outlook is good, although established orbital changes may need dedicated repair.
pitfalls: Mistaking the painless enophthalmos for an old blow-out fracture and missing the maxillary atelectasis
Attributing facial asymmetry to a neoplasm and subjecting the patient to unnecessary investigation, or conversely overlooking a genuine tumour
Failing to reconstruct a significantly depressed orbital floor after ventilating the sinus
Not recognising the diagnosis because sinonasal symptoms are conspicuously absent
references: Cummings Otolaryngology: Head and Neck Surgery
Scott-Brown's Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery
management: Endoscopic uncinectomy and middle-meatal maxillary antrostomy to re-establish maxillary sinus ventilation is the definitive treatment
Orbital floor reconstruction with an implant or graft to correct the enophthalmos and hypoglobus, often staged after ventilation is restored
Treatment of contributing osteomeatal obstruction such as polyps or mucosal disease to prevent recurrent atelectasis
Joint otolaryngology and oculoplastic or ophthalmology management to combine sinus ventilation with orbital correction
Follow-up of globe position, diplopia and facial symmetry with clinical assessment and imaging
Reassurance regarding the benign, non-inflammatory nature of the condition
